## 1. Identification Strategy
I will use a complementary, two-part strategy aligned to the two kinds of outcomes:

- Event study around the initial public disclosure of activist intent (13D filing or first press disclosure for sub-5% campaigns) to estimate the market’s assessment of the NPV to equity holders. This is the cleanest way to measure shareholder value creation at the information release.
- Staggered difference-in-differences (DID) with dynamic event-time effects to estimate causal impacts on operating performance, payouts, capital structure, and executive outcomes over 1–3 years after activism. I will implement a modern staggered-adoption estimator (Sun–Abraham via fixest’s sunab or Callaway–Sant’Anna) to address treatment-timing heterogeneity and to test pre-trends.
- Regression discontinuity (RD) around close proxy contests (cutoff at 50% support for the dissident) to estimate the causal effect of activist victory versus defeat on subsequent outcomes. This provides a powerful LATE for high-intensity activism success.

Rationale:
- Event studies are well-suited to information shocks like 13D filings and can separate equity value creation from longer-run operational changes.
- DID is appropriate because activism is staggered across firms and time; dynamic specifications can document pre-trends and post paths.
- RD in close votes provides a complementary, quasi-experimental design for the effect of “success” in high-stakes confrontations.

## 2. Treatment and Control
Treatment definitions
- Event study treatment: A firm is treated at the first public disclosure of activist intent.
  - Event date: For stakes ≥5%, the 13D filing date; for sub-5% campaigns, the earliest Factiva-verified article or Schedule 14A indicating an activist campaign.
- DID treatment: Treated firm i enters treatment in the first fiscal year (or quarter) whose end date is after the initial public disclosure date; treatment persists thereafter (intent-to-treat). We will also consider an “as-treated” variant from the first full fiscal period after public disclosure to reduce partial-period contamination.
- RD treatment (success): In campaigns culminating in a shareholder vote, treatment is activist victory; the running variable is the dissident’s vote share (or vote margin), with a cutoff at 50%.

Control groups
- Event study: Market model/Fama-French-Carhart expected return provides the benchmark; we also compute characteristic-matched buy-and-hold abnormal returns using size–book-to-market–momentum matched non-targets for robustness.
- DID: Construct a donor pool of non-targeted firms observed over the same years, excluding firms targeted at any time in the sample (“never-treated” controls). Form a matched control set using:
  - Coarsened exact matching on 3-digit SIC and size quartile.
  - Nearest-neighbor propensity-score matching (caliper) using only pre-event characteristics: size, Q, profitability, leverage, cash, payout, past returns, illiquidity, analyst coverage, institutional ownership, G-Index, and industry Herfindahl.
  - Use either matched sample DID or inverse-probability-weighted (IPW) DID on the full panel as robustness.
- RD: Local comparison of firms with dissident support just above vs. just below 50% within a symmetric bandwidth chosen by MSE-optimal procedures.

Treatment timing
- Event window definitions: [-1,+1] and [-5,+5] trading days around the event date. For robustness, [-10,+10] excluding overlapping confounders (M&A announcements, earnings).
- DID panel timing: Annual and quarterly Compustat panels; event time k relative to first public disclosure aligned to fiscal period end dates.

Running variable and cutoff (RDD)
- Running variable: Dissident vote share (or margin over management slate).
- Cutoff: 50%. Local linear RD with robust bias-corrected inference. Bandwidths chosen via rdrobust.

## 3. Key Identifying Assumptions
Event study
- Semi-strong market efficiency: Prices incorporate new information promptly. Plausible for liquid U.S. equities.
- Isolated event window: No other major firm-specific disclosures in the window that systematically coincide with activism. We will screen and exclude contaminated windows; shorter windows reduce risk.
- Correct expected return model: Use multiple models (market-adjusted, FFC4) and characteristic-matched benchmarks.

DID (staggered)
- Parallel trends: In the absence of activism, treated firms would have evolved like matched controls. Plausibility improved with rich matching and by requiring flat event-time leads; activists do target poorly performing firms, so we will explicitly check and enforce this with pre-trend tests and by incorporating pre-trend matching and firm-specific linear trends as a robustness.
- No anticipatory treatment effects: Limited leakage before public disclosure. There can be stealth accumulation; we mitigate by anchoring to first public news and testing for pre-trends at event times -4 to -1.
- No time-varying confounders differentially coincident with activism: We will drop or separately flag cases with overlapping M&A, bankruptcy, large divestitures around event time.
- SUTVA/no spillovers: Activism in one firm does not directly change outcomes in matched controls. Industry spillovers are possible; we will include industry×year fixed effects and conduct leave-one-industry-out checks.

RDD (close votes)
- Continuity: Potential outcomes vary smoothly in vote share at 50%. Reasonable in close elections.
- No precise manipulation of vote share around 50%: We will test for density discontinuities (McCrary) and covariate balance within the bandwidth.

## 4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
- Selection on unobservables and differential pre-trends (DID): Activists target firms with declining performance or latent turnaround opportunities.
  - Mitigation: Rich matching on multi-year pre-activism levels and trends; event-time leads to test for pre-trends; specification with firm-specific linear trends; synthetic control as a robustness for large targets; IPW-DID as alternative weighting scheme.
- Anticipation/leakage and confounding news (Event study and DID):
  - Mitigation: Use earliest public disclosure from Factiva/14A; exclude events with confounding announcements in [-5,+5]; shorter [-1,+1] window; “clean subsample” analysis.
- Treatment effect heterogeneity and staggered timing bias (DID):
  - Mitigation: Use Sun–Abraham or Callaway–Sant’Anna estimators; report cohort-specific and aggregated effects; avoid TWFE with naive post dummy only.
- Manipulation in proxy votes (RDD):
  - Mitigation: Density and balance tests; use narrow, data-driven bandwidths; robustness to polynomial order and bandwidth choice.

## 5. R Code Outline
Note: Illustrative; adjust file names and variable names to your schema.

```r
# Packages
library(data.table)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)       # DID with sunab
library(MatchIt)      # matching
library(WeightIt)     # IPW
library(rdrobust)     # RD
library(ggplot2)

#---------------------------
# 1) Load data
#---------------------------
act <- fread("activism_events.csv")         # firm_id, event_date, stake, hostility, tactics, 13D_flag, below5_flag
crsp <- fread("crsp_daily.csv")             # firm_id, date, ret
ff   <- fread("ff_factors_daily.csv")       # date, mktrf, smb, hml, umd, rf
comp <- fread("compustat_annual.csv")       # firm_id, fiscal_year, roa, ebitda_sales, lev, payout, cash, r_d, assets, sales, capx, q
ibes <- fread("ibes_annual.csv")            # firm_id, fiscal_year, eps_forecast
exec <- fread("execucomp_annual.csv")       # firm_id, fiscal_year, ceo_pay, ceo_turnover
irrc <- fread("irrc_gindex.csv")            # firm_id, fiscal_year, gindex
inst <- fread("institutional_ownership.csv")# firm_id, fiscal_year, inst_own
liq  <- fread("amihud_illiquidity.csv")     # firm_id, fiscal_year, amihud
perm <- fread("permno_link.csv")            # firm_id, permno

# Ensure dates are Date
act[, event_date := as.Date(event_date)]
crsp[, date := as.Date(date)]
ff[, date := as.Date(date)]

#---------------------------
# 2) Event study: CAR [-5,+5]
#---------------------------
# Merge CRSP with FF factors
crsp_ff <- merge(crsp, ff, by="date", all.x=TRUE)
crsp_ff <- merge(crsp_ff, perm, by="permno", all.x=TRUE) # permno->firm_id

# Function to compute CAR around event date
event_car <- function(fid, edate, window = c(-5, 5), est_win=c(-250,-30)) {
  df <- crsp_ff[firm_id==fid & date >= (edate + est_win[1]) & date <= (edate + window[2])]
  if (nrow(df) < 200) return(NA_real_) # need enough est obs
  df[, exret := ret - rf/100]
  # Estimation window
  est <- df[date <= (edate + est_win[2])]
  if (nrow(est) < 100) return(NA_real_)
  m <- lm(exret ~ mktrf + smb + hml + umd, data=est)
  # Event window
  ev <- df[date >= (edate + window[1]) & date <= (edate + window[2])]
  ev[, abret := exret - predict(m, newdata=ev)]
  sum(ev$abret, na.rm=TRUE)
}

# Define event date per firm: earliest public disclosure
act_earliest <- act[, .(event_date = min(event_date)), by=.(firm_id)]
# Compute CARs
cars <- act_earliest[, .(CAR_11 = event_car(firm_id, event_date, c(-5,5)),
                         CAR_3  = event_car(firm_id, event_date, c(-1,1))),
                     by=.(firm_id, event_date)]
# Summary
summary(cars$CAR_3); summary(cars$CAR_11)

#---------------------------
# 3) DID setup (annual panel)
#---------------------------
# Construct pre-treatment covariates and outcomes
panel <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y, by=c("firm_id","fiscal_year"), all=TRUE),
                list(comp, ibes, exec, irrc, inst, liq))

# Treatment cohort: first fiscal year with period end after event_date
# Need firm-year end dates
fy <- fread("firm_fy_ends.csv")  # firm_id, fiscal_year, fy_end_date
panel <- merge(panel, fy, by=c("firm_id","fiscal_year"), all.x=TRUE)
panel <- merge(panel, act_earliest, by="firm_id", all.x=TRUE)
panel[, treated := as.integer(!is.na(event_date))]
panel[, cohort := ifelse(treated==1 & fy_end_date >= event_date,
                         fiscal_year, NA_integer_)]
cohort_map <- panel[!is.na(cohort), .(cohort = min(cohort)), by=firm_id]
panel <- merge(panel, cohort_map, by="firm_id", all.x=TRUE, suffixes=c("", "_min"))
panel[, ever_treated := as.integer(!is.na(cohort_min))]

# Keep pre and post windows (e.g., ±4 years of event)
panel[, rel_year := ifelse(ever_treated==1, fiscal_year - cohort_min, NA_integer_)]

# Define controls (pre-event)
panel[, ln_assets := log(assets)]
panel <- panel[!is.na(roa) & !is.na(ln_assets)]

# Build matched control sample (using pre-period covariates, e.g., avg of t-3..t-1)
pre_cov <- panel[rel_year %between% c(-3,-1),
                 .(size_pre = mean(ln_assets, na.rm=TRUE),
                   q_pre = mean(q, na.rm=TRUE),
                   roa_pre = mean(roa, na.rm=TRUE),
                   lev_pre = mean(lev, na.rm=TRUE),
                   payout_pre = mean(payout, na.rm=TRUE),
                   inst_pre = mean(inst_own, na.rm=TRUE),
                   illiq_pre = mean(amihud, na.rm=TRUE),
                   gindex_pre = mean(gindex, na.rm=TRUE)),
                 by=.(firm_id)]
ever <- unique(panel[, .(firm_id, ever_treated)])
pre_cov <- merge(pre_cov, ever, by="firm_id", all.x=TRUE)

# Propensity score matching to define a matched control set
mdata <- na.omit(pre_cov)
m <- matchit(ever_treated ~ size_pre + q_pre + roa_pre + lev_pre + payout_pre +
               inst_pre + illiq_pre + gindex_pre,
             data=as.data.frame(mdata), method="nearest", ratio=3, caliper=0.1)
matched_ids <- data.table(firm_id = rownames(m$match.matrix))
# Create matched panel
panel_matched <- panel[firm_id %in% c(matched_ids$firm_id, cohort_map$firm_id)]

# Sun–Abraham event-study DID for ROA
# Create time variables
panel_matched[, year := fiscal_year]
panel_matched[, id := firm_id]

# Main DID: outcome = ROA
did_roa <- feols(roa ~ sunab(cohort_min, year) + q + ln_assets + lev + cash + payout |
                   id + year,  # firm and year FE
                 data = panel_matched[year %between% c(1998, 2009)], # buffer for pre/post
                 cluster = ~ id)

etable(did_roa)

# Plot dynamic effects
es <- coefplot(did_roa, keep="^sunab::", dic = dic_fixest)
print(es)

# Robustness 1: Add firm-specific linear trends
panel_matched[, t := year - min(year), by=id]
did_roa_trend <- feols(roa ~ sunab(cohort_min, year) + q + ln_assets + lev + cash + payout + i(id, t) |
                         id + year,
                       data = panel_matched, cluster=~id)

# Robustness 2: IPW-DID using WeightIt
w <- weightit(ever_treated ~ size_pre + q_pre + roa_pre + lev_pre + payout_pre +
                inst_pre + illiq_pre + gindex_pre,
              data=as.data.frame(mdata), method="ps")
w_dt <- data.table(firm_id = mdata$firm_id, w = w$weights)
panel_ipw <- merge(panel, w_dt, by="firm_id", all.x=TRUE)
panel_ipw[is.na(w), w := 1]  # controls not in pre_cov get weight 1
did_roa_ipw <- feols(roa ~ sunab(cohort_min, year) + q + ln_assets + lev + cash + payout |
                       id + year,
                     data = panel_ipw, weights=~w, cluster=~id)

#---------------------------
# 4) RDD for proxy contests
#---------------------------
# proxy.csv: firm_id, meeting_date, dissident_share (0-100), post_outcomes (e.g., ROA at t+1..t+2), covariates
proxy <- fread("proxy_contests.csv")
proxy[, running := dissident_share - 50]
# Outcome at t+2 relative to meeting (merge with compustat or pre-computed)
# Example: change in ROA from t-1 to t+2
# Assume proxy has delta_roa_t2
rd_roa <- rdrobust(y=proxy$delta_roa_t2, x=proxy$running, p=1)
summary(rd_roa)
```

Notes:
- Add screening to drop events with confounding announcements in the event window.
- Repeat DID for outcomes: EBITDA/Sales, payout ratio, net leverage, R&D intensity, CEO turnover (linear probability or Cox model), CEO pay level and pay-performance sensitivity.

## 6. Expected Results
- Shareholder value (event study): Positive announcement CARs on the order of 3–8% over [-5,+5], with larger effects for hostile campaigns, board representation pushes, breakups/spin-offs, and targets with weak governance or excess cash.
- Operating performance: ROA and EBITDA/Sales improve over 1–3 years by roughly 1–2 percentage points relative to matched controls, especially when pre-activism performance was weak.
- Payout policy: Increases in dividends/repurchases within 1–2 years; net payout ratio rises.
- Capital structure: Modest increase in leverage consistent with recapitalization and payout; improved capital allocation (lower capex/R&D where ROI is low; no uniform cut where ROI is high).
- Executive outcomes: Higher CEO turnover where pre-activism performance is poor; reduced unconditional pay but higher pay–performance sensitivity; board changes increase.
- Distributional effects: Equity gains are larger in highly levered firms and weak-governance firms; to the extent they reflect wealth transfers from creditors, we expect stronger positive stock CARs but no corresponding improvement in operating profitability. If operating metrics and analyst forecast revisions rise, that supports genuine value creation rather than pure transfers.

## 7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
Primary method assessed: staggered DID for real effects.

- C1: Parallel trends supported by pre-trend tests and rich matching = 1
- C2: No anticipatory effects before treatment = 0 (some leakage is plausible despite mitigation)
- C3: No time-varying confounders coincident with treatment = 0 (we reduce with screens and FE but cannot fully rule out)
- C4: No spillovers/SUTVA = 0 (industry spillovers possible)
- C5: Correct handling of staggered timing and heterogeneous effects (Sun–Abraham, cohort aggregation) = 1

Total: 2/5. This is why the design includes (i) an event study for market value and (ii) an RD for close votes, which together strengthen the overall causal narrative.
